messages.content:
You check whether a set of acceptance criteria still asks for what a person asked for.
Agents write acceptance criteria from a person's request, and they tend to rewrite it into
something easier to build: a word like "graph" or "across documents" disappears and nothing
notices. Your job is to notice.

Step 1. Split every quote under ASKED_BY into its distinct requirements: each separate thing
the delivered outcome must be, do or show. Split finely: "a shared map of every store that
staff can filter and print" is five requirements (a map; shared; every store; can be
filtered; can be printed). Keep the person's own nouns: a requirement named "map" stays
"map", never "list" or "view". For each requirement give:
  - id: R1, R2, ... in order;
  - requirement: a short name in the person's own words (2 to 6 words);
  - quote: the exact words from the quote that state it, copied character for character
    (keep their typos);
  - asked_by_index: the 1-based number of the ASKED_BY quote it comes from;
  - kind: "outcome" (something the delivered thing must be or do), "constraint" (a rule about
    how it is shown or built that a criterion can still check), or "process" (a statement
    about how the planning work or the acceptance criteria themselves are written, which no
    demonstration of the outcome could show). Use "process" only when no working interface
    could ever demonstrate it.
When two quotes state the same requirement, list it once and quote the clearer one.
When the user message lists REQUIREMENTS ALREADY CUT, do not split those words again: copy each
one unchanged (same id, requirement, quote, asked_by_index and kind) while its quote is still in
ASKED_BY, and cut new requirements only for words they do not cover, numbered after the highest id.

Step 2. For each requirement, decide which criteria cover it. A criterion covers a
requirement only when its criterion, demonstration or expected result would fail if the
requirement were not met. A criterion that is merely compatible with the requirement, or
that is about something nearby, does not cover it. For example a criterion "open the store
page and see every store's address" does not cover "map": a list of addresses passes it. List the
covering criterion ids, possibly none, and say why in one sentence. Then give the extent:
"full" when the listed criteria together would fail for any way of not meeting the
requirement; "partial" when they check only one part or one case of it, so something that
misses the rest still passes (say in "missing" what is left unasked); "none" when no
criterion covers it.

Step 3. If a requirement is covered by no criterion, check DEFERRALS. A requirement is
deferred only when a deferral's words, said by the person, approve leaving that requirement
out for now. Give the deferral's number, or 0 when none applies. Never treat an agent's note,
a plan or a criterion's own wording as a deferral.

Step 4. For each requirement of kind "outcome", say whether the OUTCOME line keeps it, in
substance, and why. An outcome line that says "staff look up any store" does not keep
"map", "filter" or "print".

Be strict and literal. Judge only from the text given.

ASKED_BY (the person's own words):

1. Brian, 2026-11-06: <<<on mixed mtheod work bench finsih that is not for a specific use case it is part of my broader vision>>>



REQUIREMENTS ALREADY CUT (from the last judgment):

R1 [outcome] "finish the workbench", quote 1: <<<finsih>>>

R2 [constraint] "not use-case-specific", quote 1: <<<not for a specific use case>>>

R3 [process] "part of broader vision", quote 1: <<<it is part of my broader vision>>>


OUTCOME (the agent's one-line restatement):
<<<The Mixed Methods Workbench is finished to 1.0 as a general tool in Brian's broader vision, not for one use case: on two rights-clear interview corpora a person can open a study page, follow every qualitative claim to its passage, see a quantitative strand measured and checked against the authors' own coding, read a joint display with bounded meta-inferences and a gated causal check, review and export everything with full traces, and read on a benchmark page what works, what fails and what it cost. The public PsychosisBank review stays served from committed files.>>>

CRITERIA:

[A1] 
  criterion: I can open the public review and see, for each finding, what backs it and that no causal conclusion is published yet
  demonstration: (1) Open https://psychosisbank-review.brianmills2718.workers.dev/ (2) Scroll to the 'Independent challenge' section and read each finding's card (3) Click a cited excerpt's source link 
  expected: Each finding shows its verdict, the source excerpts behind it and the remaining source gap; the page says the causal conclusion is withheld pending researcher review; the source link opens the original public document.

[A2] 
  criterion: I can see which method steps the crosswalk found shared across methods, and why
  demonstration: (1) Open the crosswalk page (planned: a table rendered from docs/research/method_decomposition/phase5/adjudication.yaml; until then the file on GitHub) (2) Read the table of groups, one row per group of steps from two or more methods (3) Open one row's justification 
  expected: 36 rows; each says same capability, shared shell or different capability with a one-line reason; today none says same capability.

[A3] 
  criterion: I can open the study page for a general example corpus and follow each qualitative claim back to the interview passage it rests on, and see the corpus is frozen with its licence
  demonstration: (1) Open proposals/open-science-study/index.html (committed; served locally with `make study-page`) (2) Read the corpus panel: 26 interviews, licence CC BY-SA 4.0, each file's hash status (3) Click a category, then one of its supporting passages (4) Read the passage in its interview, with its speaker and the author's own codes for that span 
  expected: Every interview shows 'hash matches Zenodo' in blue; each of QC's 8 categories and 6 propositions lists its passages; each passage opens at the right place in the right interview; the quantitative and integration strands say 'not built yet' in grey.

[A4] 
  criterion: I can see one category measured across every interview, and how well that measure agrees with the author's own coding on interviews it was not tuned on
  demonstration: (1) Open the study page's Measurement tab (2) Read the instrument: the rule and its included and excluded examples (3) Read the per-interview measure and the agreement figure with its interval (4) Click a disagreement and read the passage, the model's quoted reason and the author's code 
  expected: Agreement is shown with a bootstrap interval by interview and the count of held-out interviews; every disagreement is listed and opens its passage and its model trace.

[A5] 
  criterion: I can compare each qualitative proposition with the measured numbers and read whether they agree, and what may be concluded from both together
  demonstration: (1) Open the Joint display tab (2) Read one row per proposition: the claim, the measured distribution, the verdict (3) Open a row's meta-inference and its challenger's critique 
  expected: Each row shows a verdict word (converges, complements, diverges, silent) with the passages and numbers it rests on; every meta-inference says 'pending review' until reviewed.

[A6] 
  criterion: I can see a causal check on one proposition kept apart from how common it is, and that no causal conclusion shows unless the gate allows it
  demonstration: (1) Open the Causal tab (2) Read the hypothesis, each evidence test and its verdict (3) Read the publication gate line 
  expected: Process Tracing's within-case verdicts are shown in their own panel, never merged with the prevalence; the conclusion shows only when the gate says publishable, else 'withheld' and why.

[A7] 
  criterion: I can accept, reject or annotate each meta-inference, see it saved, and download one bundle with every trace
  demonstration: (1) Run `make study-workbench` and open the local address it prints (2) Accept one meta-inference and reject another with a note (3) Reload the page (4) Click 'Download bundle' and open its manifest 
  expected: Decisions survive the reload and appear in the review log; the bundle's manifest lists every file with its hash, including each run's trace and the reporting checklist.

[A8] 
  criterion: I can see on two different corpora what the workbench gets right, what it gets wrong, which planted failures it catches, and what each run cost
  demonstration: (1) Open the benchmark page (2) Read one row per corpus and strand: agreement with the authors' coding (3) Read the planted-failure table (4) Read cost and time per run with its basis 
  expected: Both corpora appear; every planted failure is listed as caught (blue) or missed (orange); costs cite their llm-cost measurement.

[A9] 
  criterion: I can see which methods the finished workbench actually runs and which it does not
  demonstration: (1) Open the method-profile page (2) Filter to 'runs in 1.0' (3) Read the reason beside an unsupported method 
  expected: Every method profile carries runs / does not run, the latter with a one-line reason; the release notes list both lists.

[A10] 
  criterion: I can point the workbench at a corpus it has never seen and get the same study page, without anyone changing its code
  demonstration: (1) Open the benchmark page's 'corpora' list and the second corpus's study page (2) Open the second corpus's study definition file (the only file added for it) (3) Read the commit that added the corpus: it changes no file under src/ 
  expected: The second corpus's study page has the same panels as the first; it was added by one study definition file plus frozen data; the page states which corpus fields were required and which were optional.


DEFERRALS:

none recorded

requirements.quote: not for a specific use case
it is part of my broader vision

mappings.coverage_reason: All ten criteria test a distinct deliverable strand of the workbench; leaving any strand unbuilt fails the criterion that covers it, so together they would fail if the workbench were not finished.
mappings.outcome_reason: The outcome says 'finished to 1.0' and enumerates every deliverable strand, keeping the requirement in full.

mappings.coverage_reason: A10 requires the workbench to accept a never-seen corpus with no code changes — it fails if the tool is hard-coded to one use case; A8 requires correct results on two distinct corpora, failing if only one is wired in.
mappings.outcome_reason: Non-outcome kind; in_outcome is true by convention.

mappings.coverage_reason: No working interface can demonstrate that a tool is part of a person's broader vision; this is a planning-context statement, not a property of the delivered product.
mappings.outcome_reason: Non-outcome kind; in_outcome is true by convention.
